findings.explanation: Phase 0 Step 3 instructs the Planner to validate 'Every section has all 15 fields listed in phase_state_schema.md §2', but the schema explicitly states 16 fields (pre_mcr_deep_pass_completed added at v0.8.0). A validator following this procedure would accept a section missing the sixteenth field as well-formed.
findings.span: Every section has all 15 fields listed in `phase_state_schema.md §2`.

findings.explanation: Phase 0 Step 3 refers to the '27-entry active enum', but the authoritative trigger enum has 30 values per phase_state_schema.md §3.1 and the frontmatter description. Triggers 28–30 would be treated as unknown and produce false TRIGGER_UNKNOWN failures.
findings.span: Every mutation-producing row in `phase_entry_log` carries a recognised `trigger` from the 27-entry active enum

findings.explanation: reviews/convergence_journal.jsonl is absent from the 'What you write' enumeration, yet Phase 5.5 requires the Planner to append journal rows there under P-7, and PHASE_PROTOCOL.md and AGENT_CONTRACTS.md confirm Planner sole-ownership. The Reflector Phase 2f out-of-contract check would incorrectly flag every P-7 journal append as a violation.
findings.span: Any Planner write outside the enumerated set above is an out-of-contract action that the Reflector's Phase 2f audit flags as `R-Refl-PC-*`.

findings.explanation: The ph2_review_completion.md description 'the Planner reads it, does not write it, but records the ph2_review_completion_signed trigger row on user approval' is ambiguous: writing the ledger row IS a write action adjacent to this artefact, potentially misleading readers about Planner passivity at Ph2 exit.
findings.span: the Planner reads it, does not write it, but records the `ph2_review_completion_signed` trigger row on user approval

findings.explanation: Neither 'What you read' nor 'What you write' explains the convergence_log.md vs convergence_journal.jsonl dual-log architecture or which is authoritative. A Planner reading only this file would not know convergence_journal.jsonl exists or is required at P-7.

MODEL_ALLOCATION.md is labelled 'v0.7.3' in 'What you read', but Phase 4.5 cites 'Opus 4.7' capability ordering which is v0.8.0-era. If the file was not updated the ordering reference is unverifiable; if it was updated the v0.7.3 label is stale and misleading.

The seed JSON template in §8.2b uses entirely old Tier-vocabulary field names (schema_version: '0.7.0', default_final_tier, t3_stale_budget_days, current_tier, tier_entry_log, prev_tier, new_tier, etc.) while the surrounding prose explicitly states these were renamed to Phase vocabulary at v0.7.0 and the document header declares v0.8.0. An agent reading both the prose contract and the seed template receives contradictory field-name instructions.

Section §10 'Lifecycle Dispatch' uses T1/T2/T3/T4 Tier vocabulary throughout its dispatch tables and sequences (T1 sub-phase 1, T2 Review & Revise, TIER_PROTOCOL.md §3.1.2, tier_entry_log, t1_pstage_declaration), while §§1–9 consistently use Ph1/Ph2/Ph3/Ph4 Phase vocabulary following the v0.7.0 rename. This creates a dual-vocabulary split in the same document.
findings.span: M1 deliverable — Project Memo (at Ph1 sub-phase 1) ... Planner (T1 bootstrap; reads classification.md for P-stage; populates t1_pstage_declaration) ... TIER_PROTOCOL.md §3.1.2

Tooling reading by header label rather than column position will break.

findings.explanation: §8.2b cross-reference paragraph describes the rename as stopping at prev_tier/new_tier ('The rename from v0.6.0's from_tier/to_tier was global'), while §8.2a states the v0.8.0 rename to prev_phase/new_phase did occur. §8.2b is therefore stale.

findings.explanation: §8.2b cites TIER_PROTOCOL.md §11 for the success-metric M3 audit and §8.3 cites TIER_PROTOCOL.md §9.1, §6, and §7.3, while §§1–9 consistently reference PHASE_PROTOCOL.md as the canonical protocol file. Both files exist but the document does not clarify their relationship; TIER_PROTOCOL.md citations in an otherwise Ph-vocabulary document are ambiguous stale references.

findings.explanation: The §3.1 regression-fix loop shows the Generator fix round looping back to Evaluator re-check with no maximum iteration count, no escalation exit condition, and no termination contract. A project could theoretically cycle indefinitely with no protocol-defined resolution.

findings.explanation: The escalation log seed template heading says '# Escalation Log — <PROJECT_NAME>' while the prose says 'The first line is always # Escalation Log — <round-id>'. These substitute different values.
Non-standard section numbering: §8 → §8.1 → §8.2 → §8.2a → §8.2b → §8.3 → §8a → §8.5 → §8.6. §8a appears as a sibling of §8 rather than a subsection, making section references unreliable.

findings.explanation: README features paragraph writes '28+ skills under skills/' (implying strictly more than 28), while the section header reads 'Skills (28)' and the filesystem contains exactly 28 skill directories. The two in-document claims are internally inconsistent.
findings.claim: 28+ skills under `skills/` (e.g. `check-contradictions`, `grounding-audit`, `narrative-structure-pass`, `run-generator-session`) with machine-checkable front matter
findings.evidence: Filesystem enumeration of skills/ yields exactly 28 subdirectories containing a SKILL.md file.

findings.explanation: The Planner is sole writer of phase_state.json, sole gatekeeper of plugin_update_proposals.md, sole resolver of model allocation, sole author of the F6 dispatch plan, sole writer of the escalation log, sole arbiter of MCR admission, and sole enforcement point for the ceiling-lock gate. Every invariant failure mode converges on a single agent with no partial-failure isolation: for example, a Phase 0.5 cache miss does not halt Phase 0.6 F6 authoring, so a stale classification can propagate into an approved dispatch plan without the user seeing the inconsistency.
findings.excerpt: The Planner carries seven orchestration responsibilities — (i) classification; (ii) revision planning; (iii) dispatch of Evaluator/Generator/Reflector; (iv) sole-writer ownership of reviews/tier_state.json; (v) model-capability arbitration; (vi) MCR compilation and Ph4 admission control; (vii) user-checkpoint gating.

findings.explanation: AGENT_CONTRACTS.md §1 Planner 'Outputs (write)' lists only three artifacts (classification.md, revision_plan.md, dispatch instructions), while planner.md §Output Contract enumerates at least fifteen distinct artifact paths. AGENT_CONTRACTS.md is stated as the authority that wins on conflicts, yet its Planner output list is radically incomplete. The Reflector's contract-verification check cannot reliably audit for out-of-contract writes if the contract omits most of the actual write surface.

The seed template in AGENT_ORCHESTRATION.md §8.2b uses old Tier-vocabulary field names throughout (schema_version: '0.7.0', default_final_tier, tier_entry_log, etc.) while planner.md Phase 0 and PHASE_PROTOCOL.md require v0.8.0 Phase vocabulary. A Planner bootstrapping from this template will produce a ledger that fails Phase 0 Step 3 well-formedness validation or silently triggers the migration path rather than the fresh-project path.

The Planner's session-state cache is explicitly never persisted and emits only an advisory transcript note on invalidation. If the session ends abnormally after the cache was built but before the invalidation advisory was emitted, the Reflector at the next session has no way to determine whether the prior session's cache was stale. The R-Refl-Cache-1 audit check depends on a durable signal that the spec explicitly says is never written.
findings.excerpt: If the on-disk hash differs, the cache is stale — invalidate the entry and re-read, and emit an advisory [CACHE-INVALIDATED-EXTERNAL-WRITE: <path>] note... The cache does not persist across session boundaries and is never serialised to .cache/ or any other on-disk location.

findings.explanation: Phase 4.5 step-by-step prose still describes an independent model-resolution workflow (read MODEL_ALLOCATION.md, resolve per agent) that contradicts the v0.7.4 P-1 end-note requiring the Planner to consume the pre-authored F6 model allocation from Phase 0.6 unchanged. An agent following Phase 4.5 steps before reading the end-note will execute the pre-F6 workflow and may resolve a different model than Phase 0.6 pre-authorized, triggering R-Refl-DP-1 without any procedural error.
findings.excerpt:
### Phase 4.5 — Model-dispatch resolution (v0.7.3)
1. **Read MODEL_ALLOCATION.md.** Load the allocation table in §2...
2. **Resolve per dispatched agent.** For each agent you will spawn in this cycle, look up the row for the section's current_phase and take the model string from §2.

findings.explanation: The convergence_log.md / convergence_journal.jsonl contract split (P-4) has no cross-validation gate during the Ph3 round. The two files have different intended content and no check — before or after Phase 5.5 — verifies they are in sync. A convergence_log.md row with no corresponding journal line (or vice versa) can persist silently through all of Ph3, making the audit trail unreliable for the entire convergence history.
findings.excerpt: **Primary deliverable (contract-split at v0.7.4, P-4...)** A two-file artefact set: reviews/convergence_log.md retains Trajectory-synthesis prose... reviews/convergence_journal.jsonl carries the per-iteration mechanical state.

findings.explanation: The F6 checks_scheduled[] ceiling cannot expand mid-round without a full Planner interrupt, fresh F6 authoring, and user re-approval. A mid-round discovery of a condition warranting an additional check has no lightweight escalation path, which may cause maintainers to systematically under-schedule checks to avoid the friction.
findings.excerpt: The Evaluator and Reflector read this list at their Phase-0 bootstrap and treat it as the ceiling of checks to run — expanding beyond it requires a fresh F6 with modifications_recorded: true.

findings.explanation: Escalation log header template uses old prev_tier/new_tier column vocabulary while v0.8.0 normative spec renamed these to prev_phase/new_phase. Parser-compatible by column position but breaks any tooling reading by header label.
findings.excerpt: | timestamp | prev_tier -> new_tier | gate | reason | round_id |

findings.explanation: Phase 0 Step 3 still says '15 fields' while the frontmatter, Output Contract, and schema all say '16 fields' (pre_mcr_deep_pass_completed added at v0.8.0). The bootstrap check will silently accept malformed v0.8.0 ledger rows missing this field.
findings.excerpt: Every section has all 15 fields listed in `phase_state_schema.md §2`.

findings.explanation: Ph3-STALE default threshold is stated as 14 days in planner.md Phase 0 step 6 and the AGENT_ORCHESTRATION.md seed template, but 90 days in PHASE_PROTOCOL.md §3.3. A project inactive for 30 days may or may not receive [Ph3-STALE] depending on which document the current Planner session resolved first, creating non-deterministic MCR admission blocking.
findings.excerpt: If delta > ph3_staleness_budget (default 14 days), surface the advisory [Ph3-STALE]
